title: Gougere
subtitle: French choux buns baked with gruyere
excerpt: Gruyere-enriched choux pastry piped into rounds and baked until puffed, hollow, and deeply golden. Crisp on the outside, airy within, and best eaten straight from the oven.
sourceNotes: Burgundian French tradition, adapted from standard French patisserie method.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze unbaked piped portions on a lined tray, then transfer to a bag. Bake from frozen, adding 5 minutes to the bake time.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the recipe and freeze half the unbaked portions for another day.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Pipe and refrigerate unbaked gougeres for up to 4 hours. Bake just before serving.

content.text: Gougeres are savoury choux buns from Burgundy, puffed and golden with gruyere melted through the dough. The key is adding the eggs slowly to reach the right consistency. Once baked, eat them quickly while the outside stays crisp.
Heat the oven to 200C. Line a baking tray with baking paper.
Put the water, butter, and salt in a saucepan over a medium heat. Bring to a full boil, making sure the butter has melted completely.

Remove from the heat. Tip in the flour all at once and beat vigorously with a wooden spoon until the mixture forms a smooth ball that pulls away from the sides of the pan. Return to a low heat and stir for 1 minute to dry the paste out slightly.
Transfer the paste to a bowl. Beat in the eggs a little at a time, beating well after each addition. The dough should be thick and glossy and drop slowly from the spoon when lifted.
Stir in three quarters of the gruyere, the mustard if using, and the black pepper.
Spoon or pipe rounds of dough about 3cm in diameter onto the lined tray, spacing them 4cm apart. Scatter the remaining cheese over the tops.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until deep golden and puffed. Do not open the oven in the first 20 minutes. Serve warm immediately.

items.symptom: The gougeres collapse after coming out of the oven.
items.cause: They were underbaked or the oven was opened too early.
items.fix: Bake until deeply golden all over. The colour should be a proper bronze, not pale gold. Pierce one with a skewer after baking to help steam escape.

items.symptom: The dough is too runny to hold a shape.
items.fix: Add the egg very gradually and stop when the dough just holds a soft peak that slowly topples. You may not need all the egg.

items.symptom: The buns are dense and did not puff.
items.cause: The paste was not beaten long enough to incorporate air, or the oven was too cool.
items.fix: Beat the paste thoroughly after each addition of egg, and make sure the oven is fully up to temperature before the tray goes in.
